drafts.title: Hypothetical VRAM Planning Checklist for 12GB GPUs (LocalLLaMA)
drafts.body:
This guide outlines a hypothetical VRAM planning checklist for users with a 12 GB GPU running local language models. It's crucial to remember this is a theoretical exercise, not based on actual tested models or runtimes. We'll break down VRAM usage into three key areas: model weights, the KV cache, and other runtime allocations.  Understanding these components is vital for efficient local LLM deployment.

Model weights represent the largest portion of VRAM. The size of the model directly dictates how much space it occupies. The KV cache, used during inference for attention mechanisms, grows dynamically with context length. Finally, other runtime allocations include the operating system, the LLM framework itself, and any auxiliary processes.  This checklist aims to provide a structured approach to estimating VRAM needs in a hypothetical scenario, helping you gauge potential model compatibility and performance before committing to a specific setup. No actual models or runtimes were tested in developing this guide.

drafts.title: A Theoretical VRAM Allocation Framework for 12GB Local LLM Setups
drafts.body:
This document presents a hypothetical framework for VRAM planning on a 12 GB GPU for local language models. All scenarios discussed are purely theoretical and have not been validated through actual testing. The objective is to provide a structured method for anticipating resource needs. We will delineate VRAM usage into three distinct categories: static model weight storage, dynamic KV cache requirements, and miscellaneous runtime overhead.  This separation helps in understanding where VRAM is consumed during LLM operation.

Model weights are the foundational data, consuming a fixed amount of VRAM based on the model's architecture and precision. The KV cache, essential for efficient text generation, scales with the input sequence length and batch size. Other runtime allocations encompass the Python interpreter, libraries like PyTorch or TensorFlow, CUDA kernels, and system processes. This theoretical checklist serves as a preliminary guide to help assess feasibility for different models on a 12GB card, acknowledging that no specific models or runtimes were benchmarked.
